ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Immune-mediated rather than direct microbial injury

A patient with viral hepatitis has scattered dying hepatocytes adjacent to activated CD8 T lymphocytes. The lymphocytes recognize viral peptides displayed on hepatocyte MHC class I molecules. Which mechanism best explains this component of hepatocyte injury?

  1. Cytotoxic lymphocyte induction of death in infected host cells
  2. Direct enzymatic digestion by bacterial exotoxin
  3. Reduced inspired oxygen concentration
  4. Loss of hemoglobin from all circulating erythrocytes
  5. Mechanical disruption by extracellular parasites
Answer and explanation

Cytotoxic lymphocyte induction of death in infected host cells

Antigen-specific T cells can eliminate infected cells through cytotoxic pathways.

Option explanations

Cytotoxic lymphocyte induction of death in infected host cells: Antigen-specific T cells can eliminate infected cells through cytotoxic pathways.

Direct enzymatic digestion by bacterial exotoxin: The case describes T-cell recognition of a viral antigen, not a bacterial toxin.

Reduced inspired oxygen concentration: No environmental oxygen deficiency is described.

Loss of hemoglobin from all circulating erythrocytes: Anemia does not explain antigen-specific lymphocyte contact.

Mechanical disruption by extracellular parasites: No parasitic invasion is described.
